- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid missing downside reversal.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in the following 5–7 days; apply a “cool-down” correction of 2–5% to prevent overreaction.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 30-day moving average), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if model’s first 3–5 days are significantly above true outcome, it’s likely overconfident; apply a “lag correction” by subtracting 0.5–1.5% from early forecast values.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 2–3 swings in 10 days), model often misjudges direction; align forecast with sentiment’s most recent dominant trend (not average).
